title: The Hanger Club with Booker Coleman, 1936
summary: After the Ridgely club folded Phillips played about six months with Booker Coleman at the Hanger Club near the Fourteenth Street Bridge, July to winter 1936.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I stayed with him for about a year. Then the man folded the club up. The club folded up. Then after that, I went with Booker Coleman. I went up to a club around here called the Hanger Club. That's out there right across the Fourteenth Street Bridge. There used to be an airport there, years ago.
You mean out there by the South Capitol Street Bridge, out by where Bowling Air Force Base used to be?
No. Right out by the Fourteenth Street Bridge. The old bridge? I don't know whether it's still there. Maybe they tore it down now. There used to be an old
bridge, before they had the other one.
You mentioned the airport was there.
It was then. Wasn't much of an airport then.
The other one wasn't built until around 1940.
You were talking playing at the Hanger Club with Booker Coleman.

Yeah, we went over there with Booker, stayed over there about six months, I guess. That's where the jobs was in them days. You didn't stay nowhere long. Not here in Washington. We stayed there for about six months -- the Hanger Club.
That first job lasted how long?
I went there in 1935, and left in about June 1936. Then in July of '36, I went with Booker over to the Hanger Club.
And that lasted another six months, from July of '36 all the way up to the winter of '36.
